SMTO-EXE-0153 — SMTO couldn't find that spot on the screen

GUID: 17b26d09-1f5a-5c79-8fc0-e53552b047d1
Slug: ui-invalid-coordinate-space
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO tried to point at a screen position that isn't inside any current screen or inside the chosen window, so it didn't click or move anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway's computer, make sure the window SMTO is working in is still open, not minimized, and fully on a screen. SMTO measures positions inside that window; if it shrank, moved or closed, the spot falls outside it.
  2. If monitors were added, removed or rearranged, or display scaling changed, ask SMTO to take a new look at the screen before it clicks. Screen positions come from the current monitor layout, so positions found earlier no longer line up.
  3. Ask SMTO to click the button or field by its name instead of by screen position. Using the app's own controls avoids screen-position math entirely.

What success looks like

  • SMTO clicks the intended place and the expected change appears in the app.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer. Mention how many monitors it has and which app SMTO was using.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Desktop UI service rejected a point because its coordinate space lacked a required window_id or display_id, is unsupported on this platform (global screen_physical on macOS), or maps outside the current display or window client bounds.

What this means

  • Coordinate translation lacked required display/window identity, used a space unsupported by the platform, or mapped outside current display/client bounds. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Coordinate translation lacked required display/window identity, used a space unsupported by the platform, or mapped outside current display/client bounds.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare coordinate_space, display_id/window_id, scale and current bounds; do not assume a global physical-pixel mapping on macOS.

How to fix it

  • Send screen_physical global coordinates (Windows/Linux), display-local screen_logical coordinates with a Screen display_id, or window_client coordinates with a window_id that fall inside the current client rectangle; on macOS use logical points because no global physical mapping exists. Re-read display geometry after monitor, scaling or window-size changes.
  • Use explicit screen_physical global coordinates, display-local screen_logical with a Screen display_id, or a supported window_client point. macOS accepts logical points; no global physical mapping is assumed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use explicit screen_physical global coordinates, display-local screen_logical with a Screen display_id, or a supported window_client point. macOS accepts logical points; no global physical mapping is assumed.

How to verify the fix

  • The explicit point maps inside the intended current display or client area before input.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
